answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a challenge-bound sequence of modular squarings before receiving a valid Wesolowski proof. Because each squaring depends on the prior result, GPUs cannot shorten one chain through parallel computation; creating many clones requires separate chains and proportionally more elapsed time or hardware. Like an ocean current tracing a spiral around timber, the work advances step by step: costly to multiply identities, though not an absolute bar to well-resourced attackers.
